messages.subject: Predictions
parts: This might be more of a statistics question but I'll throw it out there just in case someone has any ideas... I'm using an unmarked ZIP model to predict values of abundance on hypothetical situations during which I hold all input parameters at their average values and only vary the parameter of interest (All continuous variables were standardized to 0 prior to analysis).  I have two categorical variables in my analysis though - both of which are involved in separate interactions.  Does anyone know how to hold these categorical values at their "average"?  Even if I put zero for all the parameters, the intercept still represents the reference variable....not really sure how to handle that - any advice would be appreciated!

messages.author: dc8b4131b39a099f
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Predictions
parts:
I dont think you can hold your cat variables at a mean, but if the interactions are "significant" according to your criteria, then you could estimate and report abundance across some gradient of your continuous variables for each level of your categorical variables.  Otherwise, you can just estimate abun across your continuous var gradients for any level of your cat vars because they do not vary based on your criteria.

Example using AICcmodavg, where YPM (cont) and MT (cat) interact, and area is a cont offset variable:

DF=data.frame(MT=rep(c("NB","NH","NNH"),each=9),YPM=seq(1,9,1),AREA=10)
pred=predictSE.zip(YPM.INT.MT,newdata=DF,se.fit=TRUE,parm.type="lambda",type="response",c.hat=1,print.matrix=FALSE)
abun=pred$fit
LCL=pred$fit-(pred$se.fit*1.435)
UCL=pred$fit+(pred$se.fit*1.435)
matrix(data=c(LCL,abun,UCL),ncol=3)

# change intercept level for MT
siteCovs(umf)$MT=relevel(siteCovs(umf)$MT,ref="NH")
